## p228 A — Aviation staff and army aviation park march destinations

**Edition context:** 30 November: aviation march destinations.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov30-aviation-march-destination-november-30-aviation-march-destinations"></a>



Printed **p228 A** reports proposed march destinations for an aviation staff and a numerically limited army aviation park. Its native body has **384 occupied slots**, although the questioned advertised count is **RICHI-374?**. A conditional 374-coordinate frame yields a largely readable body. Seven observed-coordinate substitutions and four printed-mask fills support the proposed word reading.

The ten-coordinate exclusion is a substantive model choice. All **ten** equally priced contiguous placements remain in the evidence. The primary representation removes two complete printed groups and preserves the source’s repetitions in the native layer; it does not establish how the surplus arose historically.

Research and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The published Nov28–Dec1 key retains the credit of George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Earlier source surveys and OCR retain their attribution; no first historical decipherment is claimed.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov30-aviation-march-destination-what-the-geometry-search-establishes"></a>

### Results and limits of the geometry search

The search uses eight retrospective word spans at the offsets listed below. It does not constrain the references, other surrounding words or the entire proposed body. It prices observed-coordinate conflicts, recording mask fills and source exclusions separately.

All **375 contiguous ten-slot exclusions** were tested. The minimum is **seven observed substitutions**, at starts **4–13** inclusive. These are all retained, not just the six source maps yielding the primary ciphertext.

A second, narrower source-group model tests all **2,850 pairs of complete five-coordinate groups** among the first 76 groups. The final four-coordinate group is retained. Exactly two pairs attain the same seven-substitution minimum: zero-based groups **[1,2]** and **[2,3]**, corresponding to source intervals **[5,15)** and **[10,20)**. They remove the intervening -XVVG and one of the repeated VGXXV groups and produce the same shortened ciphertext.

These two whole-group descriptions support selecting a reproducible primary display. They do not prove a unique historical deletion, nor exclude other damage models. All words and offsets were chosen retrospectively; this is not a blind decipherment test.

| Contiguous exclusion start | Source glyphs excluded | Raw fixed / edited fixed | Difference outside the eight word spans |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 4 | 9 valid + 1 masked | 183 / 187 | GEDTATET, rather than the primary GEDRATET |
| 5–10 | 9 valid + 1 masked | 183 / 187 | Same primary ciphertext and reading; six distinct origin maps |
| 11 | 10 valid | 182 / 186 | MAR?CHZ instead of MARSCHZ; the retained source10 mask stays unfilled |
| 12–13 | 10 valid | 182 / 186 | MAR?CHZ and FUEM instead of MARSCHZ and FUER |

All four descriptions above still cost seven observed substitutions and four stencil-directed mask fills. The start 11–13 branches retain a fifth source mask outside the selected words. Its complete six-coordinate domain and exact full-ciphertext witnesses remain in the certificate; it is not silently filled to improve the prose.

The seven observed changes are **98 F→V, 133 X→V, 165 F→V, 186 F→V, 225 G→D, 233 G→D and 234 F→V**. The four mask fills are **25 -→D, 52 M→D, 57 M→D and 117 -→X**. These are separate from the nine valid and one masked source slots excluded by the frame.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — primary frame, seven observed substitutions and four printed-mask fills:**

```text
KOFLXXYZUDORTXJ43YX4OPISTANKOGENLUFTGEDRATETXYMARSCHZIELFUERSTABKOFLMACKYBUCKARESTJYMARSCHZYFUERZAHLENMAESSIGBESCHRAENKTENARMEEFLUGPARKPLOESTIYANDERBAHNKRONSTADTBUCARESTYKOFLMACKYJYX4OPYY
```

</details>

**Readable German — the complete primary edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Kofl XX. Zu dort X J43. X4 OP ist an Kogenluft gedratet X. Marschziel fuer Stab Kofl Mack. Buckarest J. Marschz. Fuer zahlenmaessig beschraenkten Armeeflugpark Ploesti. An der Bahn Kronstadt Bucarest. Kofl Mack. J. X4 OP.

**Conditional interpretation — aviation movement arrangements:**

The proposed body gives Buckarest as the march destination for the staff marked KOFL MACK and Ploesti for a numerically restricted army aviation park, followed by a railway reference to Kronstadt and Bucarest. It also refers to an earlier communication to KOGENLUFT. This reading does not identify a specific historical order, establish its execution, or expand the aviation abbreviations into independently verified offices.

GEDRATET is retained without inserting an H, BUCKAREST is retained beside the later BUCAREST, and MARSCHZ is not expanded. J43, X4OP, J, X and XX remain literal numeral/letter labels. No date, reference number or personal identity is inferred from them. The conditional reading’s ordinary words do not resolve the competing layouts outside the stated eight spans.

## Demobilization at Neuhof, south of Fulda

**Sources on this page:** p228 B1, p228 B3.

<a id="edition-cases-military-neuhof-demobilization-demobilization-at-neuhof-south-of-fulda"></a>



**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The opening of this three-part telegram directs a Flak unit, whose number
remains unresolved, toward demobilization at **Neuhof, south of Fulda**.
The middle part now supports a conditional continuation naming the Hanau–Fulda
line, enclosures 1 and 2, and formations undergoing demobilization within a
deputy command's district. The final part explicitly directs the relevant
field-army items to Neuhof.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p228, PDF page 231](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [preserved section](../../experiments/neuhof_demobilization/sources/p228_B.png)
appears under `30th NOVEMBER, 1918.` with the header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) ZON v BSL (01.33 a.m., December 1st)
NO 152 1512 3 TLE
```

</details>

All three parts use the unchanged published `Nov28-Dec1` square and ranks.
The source edition retains raw `Y` separators, numeral labels and rare
letters. The separate shared interpretation below supplies part of B1's
numerical fields.

<a id="edition-cases-military-neuhof-demobilization-b1-the-destination-instruction"></a>

### B1: the destination instruction

The first part advertises `RICHI-246` and has exactly **246 slots**, including
six printed dashes. Its earlier OCR stream had 241 coordinates and did not
produce a coherent reading. The visual transcription gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
0OKXXYYZUMERLYVJXYXXZX4NRP680YX4GEHYAY3YANLGYXLF?YNRYX4SPALTE9FLAKABTEILUNG?0WIRDNI?L3NDARMJT?DTSONDERNINYNEU?OFYSUEDHFUL?A
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions and five fills of printed dashes give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
AOKXXYYZUMERLYVJXYXXZX4NRP680YX4GEHYAY3YANLGYXLFDYNRYX4SPALTE9FLAKABTEILUNG?0WIRDNICHINDARMSTADTSONDERNINYNEUHOFYSUEDLFULDA
```

</details>

The ordinary body names a Flak unit and places its destination at Neuhof,
south of Fulda, with Darmstadt appearing in the negative part of the
instruction. It retains the shortened `NICHIN`: the expected German phrase
would normally contain `NICHT IN`, but no `T` is inserted into the fixed
source frame. The Flak unit field remains `?0`. Its number, the order
number, date-like fields and column-reference label remain uninterpreted.

The [joint calendar and unit interpretation](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
adds `GA=0` and `VG=7`, fixing three more numeral positions without additional
source changes:

| Field | Published-key labels | Joint interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Order reference | `P680` | **P067** |
| Flak unit field | `?0` | **?7** |

This interpreted layer fixes **120/123 positions**. The leading unit character
remains an erasure, and two other fields retain the shared `4/5` ambiguity.
The body continues into the middle part with the demobilization wording.

<a id="edition-cases-military-neuhof-demobilization-b2-the-demobilization-continuation"></a>

### B2: the demobilization continuation

The [current B2 edition](#edition-cases-military-p228-demobilization-fragment) reaches **125/132
positions** through a conditional relocation of five printed mask slots,
word proposals and two shared-reference transfers from B1. It preserves all
221 observed coordinates in their original relative order. Five observed
substitutions and 36 mask fills support the combined reading; seven positions,
including the command field and the prefix before `CKFORMATIONEN`, remain
unresolved.

<details>
<summary>Earlier native-frame opening</summary>

The second part advertises `RICHI-264` and has **264 slots**, including
**43 printed dashes**. Its direct label reading is:


</details>

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

```text
ANSTRECKEHANAUFULDADEMOBILGEMACHT
```

</details>

It says “demobilized on the Hanau-Fulda line.” This is a conditional

confined to these 33 plaintext positions.

The remaining **99 positions** retain their source-derived labels and

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-military-neuhof-demobilization-b3-routing-to-neuhof"></a>

### B3: routing to Neuhof

The source heading is literally **`RICHI-196?`**. Counting the received
groups gives **186 slots**, including one printed dash. The edition uses
that actual 186-slot frame and preserves the questioned header length.
It does not insert ten hypothetical coordinates. Its direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DESFELDHEERESSINDDAHERNICHTNACHDAR?SADTSONDERNNACHNEUHOFZULEITENYCMTRUPPENDEPY3025YXXYX4YAY3Y
```

</details>

Filling the one printed dash at source index **15**, group **4**, coordinate
**1**, with `X` gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DESFELDHEERESSINDDAHERNICHTNACHDARMSADTSONDERNNACHNEUHOFZULEITENYCMTRUPPENDEPY3025YXXYX4YAY3Y
```

</details>

The final instruction says the relevant field-army items must therefore
be directed to Neuhof. The preceding plural subject lies in the unread
middle portion, so the edition does not invent a specific unit or equipment
category. The city string remains `DARMSADT`, without an added `T`.
The office label `CMTRUPPENDEP` and its numerical reference remain literal.

The published key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).

work adds the exact source edition, the readable opening instruction and
the separately limited middle proposal. No explicit p228 B example was
located in the bounded author-paper, supplementary-reading and catalog
check; no universal first-decipherment claim is made.

## p228 B2 — Neuhof demobilization continuation: deputy-command district and formations

**Edition context:** p228 B2 — Demobilization district and formations.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p228-demobilization-fragment-p228-b2--demobilization-district-and-formations"></a>


[The three-part Neuhof telegram](#edition-cases-military-neuhof-demobilization)

**Recovery and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 4 November 2026.**
Moving five printed mask slots exposes a substantial continuation of the
Neuhof demobilization instruction. The unchanged 28 November–1 December key
fixes **90/132 raw positions** in this conditional frame. The word proposal
fixes **121/132 positions**, comprising **95 proposed word positions** and
26 retained labels in other fields. Its five observed-coordinate substitutions
and 32 printed-mask fills are individually recorded.

Two shared-reference steps now extend that proposal to **125/132 positions**:
the first part supplies the order suffix and the first enclosure number.
Together with the later numeral interpretation, the latter passage reads
**Anlg. 1 u. 2**. Both steps use complete original donor pairs and add four
mask fills, with no additional observed-coordinate substitution.

The earlier edition proposed only the first 33 positions. This continuation
adds the phrases `DIE NACH ANLG`, `DES ERL`, `IM BEREICH DES STELLV`,
`DEMOBILMACHENDEN` and the suffix `FORMATIONEN`. The intervening command
designation and the prefix `???CK` remain unresolved.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p228-demobilization-fragment-readable-fragments"></a>

### Readable fragments

**Conditional interpretation — readable German after the shared-reference and enclosure transfers, with the declared numeral interpretation; ellipses omit fields shown below:**

> An Strecke Hanau–Fulda demobil gemacht. Die nach Anlg. 1 u. 2 des Erl. […] im Bereich des stellv. […] demobilmachenden ???CKformationen […]

The wording concerns formations undergoing demobilization within a deputy
command's district and refers to two enclosures and an order. The incomplete
compound ending in `FORMATIONEN` does not identify a specific formation type.
The [third part](#edition-cases-military-neuhof-demobilization-b3-routing-to-neuhof) continues with
`DESFELDHEERES` and directs the relevant items toward Neuhof. The new fragment
helps connect the instruction's two previously readable ends; it does not
supply the remaining reference values or establish that the order was executed.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p228-demobilization-fragment-source-and-frame"></a>

### Source and frame

Childs, printed p228 / PDF page 231, section B2, `2 TL RICHI-264`, under
`30th NOVEMBER, 1918.` The parent header reads
`B) ZON v BSL (01.33 a.m., December 1st); NO 152 1512 3 TLE`.
The body contains exactly **264 slots: 221 observed coordinates and 43 dashes**.

<details>

```text
AGAVX XAGDD FGFAA GAXXV ADDFG FGVFX VVGGG FDGAV
XGVXD DXXFA AXFGV XDVGD DAGGV FAAAX FDAGV VDDGV
GVGGA FFDGA -AVVG FGVFG DVXAG XFXGG GFGFG ADXFV

----- ----- ----- ----- DFGFF VAAVX XGFFD FGFFV
```

All indices are zero based, with end-exclusive ranges. Remove the existing
five printed masks at source[195:200], then insert them at boundary246 of

This is a conditional placement of a printed mask group, not an OCR correction.
Any five contiguous masks starting at source192 through215 give the same

The 11 unresolved positions are **44,45,60,61,68,92,93,94,116,117,118**.
The three positions before `CKFORMATIONEN` are deliberately unfilled.
The known numeral labels, `Y` labels and `X4AK` field are not assigned
historical numbers by this edition. A complete arbitrary re-encryption
witness checks the arithmetic without claiming the remaining erased values.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p228-demobilization-fragment-shared-reference-and-enclosure-witnesses"></a>

### Shared reference and enclosure witnesses

The first part has the fully observed reference fragment `P680YX4GEH`;
B2 has `2680Y??GEH`. If these denote the same order-reference field,
B1 supplies the two missing labels `X4` at B2 positions 60–61. The
[separate certificate](../../experiments/p228_demobilization_fragment/reference_witness.json)
records the original donor pairs `GX` and `GD`, fills source255 with `G`
and source210 with `D`, and verifies both parts under the same unchanged key.
This optional layer reaches **123/132 fixed positions**, with **34 printed-mask
fills and the same five observed substitutions**. The primary layer stays at
121/132. The observed `P` versus `2` disagreement is retained; neither label
receives a numerical interpretation. These are separate parts with a proposed
shared reference, not duplicate receptions. Reproduce with
`python experiments/p228_demobilization_fragment/verify_reference.py --verify`.

The first part also has the fully observed `ANLGYX`. Its two final pairs,
`AX` and `GX`, fit B2's `ANLG??UJ` at positions 44–45. Transferring them fills
source253 with `A` and source208 with `X`, producing `ANLGYXUJ`. This
**enclosure extension fixes 125/132 positions**, with five observed
substitutions and 36 mask fills in total. Positions 68, 92–94 and 116–118
remain unresolved.

Under the [shared calendar and unit interpretation](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md),
the enclosure field reads `ANLGX1U2`, and B2's order reference reads
`3067X18GEH`. B1 has `P067X18GEH`; that initial P/3 disagreement remains.

## Late-November cipher and routing instructions — pp225–228

<a id="late-november-cipher-and-routing-instructions--p225228"></a>

**Sources on this page:** p228 C1, p228 C2.

**Related source pages:** [p225 A](225.md#source-p225-a), [p226 B2](226.md#source-p226-b2), [p227 B](227.md#source-p227-b).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-late-november-cipher-and-routing-instructions--p225228"></a>



**Source reading and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Published period keys: George Lasry and collaborators.**

Five ciphertext records and one cleartext notice describe missing December key tables, proposed sharing of keys, a fragment of a numerical-code instruction, and direct routing to an army station. All ciphertext below is read with the unchanged published **Nov28–Dec1** key. These messages give evidence about specific communications arrangements; they do not assign a key to an unresolved challenge.

| Record | Received slots | Fixed raw positions, including garbles | Content |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| p225 A | 232 | 110/116; completed 116/116 | UKS to use a November key from 1 December because December tables have not arrived |
| p226 B2 | 208 | 104/104 | Surviving continuation about reading numerical sequences backwards |
| p227 B | 152 | 76/76 | Send messages for the army and subordinate formations directly to ZOEN |
| p228 C1 | 176 | 88/88 | Agreement involving UKS, ZOEN and BSL about the December key |
| p228 C2 | 144 | 72/72 | BSL and UKS should use the same key; UKS agrees |
| p227 C | Cleartext | Not a decipherment | ITOCHI parts cannot be deciphered; request RICHI or plaintext |

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-an-explicit-agreement-to-use-the-same-key"></a>

### An explicit agreement to use the same key

p228 C is headed `BSL v ZON` (the O has two marks), `04.47 a.m., December 1st`, `0420 (11/30) 2 TLE`. Both parts are directly readable without any coordinate repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — two separate source parts under the unchanged key:**

```text
p228 C1
MITYUKSYVEREINBARTEYZOENYDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELWIEYBSLYZWISCHENYBSLYUNDYZOENYVORGESCHLAGENYY

p228 C2
IMVERKEHRYBSLYUNDYUKSYGLEICHENSCHLUESSELVERWENDENYYUKSYISTEINVERSTANDENY
```

</details>

The first part reports an arrangement with UKS concerning the December key as proposed between BSL and ZOEN. The second is explicit: use the same key in BSL–UKS traffic, and UKS agrees. Together, the two source streams retain **320/320 coordinates** and directly fix **160/160 plaintext positions**. This does not establish which particular November day's key the parties subsequently used. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p228_C.png).

### November key reused because December tables are missing

**Readable German — six compatible fills and two word repairs:**

> Station UKS chiffr. ab ersten Dez. mit NSL Nov., da Dez.-Tafeln noch nicht
> eingegangen. Bitte Telegr. an uns ebenfalls mit NSL Nov. schluesseln.

UKS reports that December tables have not arrived and requests reciprocal
use of the material labelled `NSL NOV` from 1 December. The two occurrences
of `NSL` are retained. The abbreviation does not identify a particular
November day's key.

The notice is headed `BSL v UKS (09.24 p.m., November 28th)`,
`2200 (28/11)`, `RIZI-232`. Its native frame has **232 slots**, including
five printed dashes and the invalid `R` in `DFGVR`. Six compatible word fills
complete **116/116 positions** while retaining all **226 valid coordinates**.
Reading `NICGT` as `NICHT` and `TELEGD` as `TELEGR` costs two additional
observed-coordinate substitutions. The quotation uses that edited layer,
with editorial spacing and punctuation.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-numerical-code-fragment-and-army-routing"></a>

### Numerical-code fragment and army routing

p226 B2 says that its first part is missing. The surviving continuation directly gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZAHLENREIHENVONRUECKWAERTSGELESENYSODASSXYXSZ8HLEN3Y5Y9YX5YX0YUYSYWYYBENUTZENSIEGLEICHESMITUNFYANTWORTYY
```

</details>

The beginning says that numerical sequences are read backwards; the end asks the recipient to use the same procedure in communication with the sender and to answer. `Z8HLEN → ZAHLEN` and `MITUNF → MITUNS` cost two coordinate substitutions. The central examples, including `XYXS` and `3Y5Y9YX5YX0`, remain literal. The missing first part and those garbles prevent reconstruction of a complete numerical-code rule. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p226_B2.png).

p227 B directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BITTEFUNKSPRUECHEANXXYARMEEUNDUNTERSTEL6TEFORMATIONENUNMITTELBARANZOENGEBENY
```

</details>

Restoring `UNTERSTELLTE` costs one coordinate substitution. The raw army field **`XX`** is retained, without silently treating it as an Arabic number or Roman numeral. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p227_B.png).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-separate-historical-interpretation-of-the-army-field"></a>

### Separate historical interpretation of the army field

The later [unit-based key-label review](../../experiments/late_key_interpretation/README.md) applies the optional p230 map to p227 B. Baseline `X→1` and the separate `Y→X` separator convention give **11th Army**; with the already counted one-coordinate repair of `UNTERSTELLTE`, the instruction asks for telegrams to the 11th Army and subordinate formations to be sent directly to ZOEN. The baseline text above remains the unchanged-key result. Applying the same declared layers to p226 B2 leaves its numerical examples damaged and does not recover the missing code rule.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-late-november-cipher-instructions-a-cleartext-request-to-avoid-an-unreadable-cipher"></a>

### A cleartext request to avoid an unreadable cipher

p227 C, headed `BSL v UKS`, `2316 (11/28) K. M. BERLIN`, says that parts 3 and 4 of a referenced War Department message in **ITOCHI** cannot be deciphered. It requests **RICHI or plaintext**, then asks that ciphering be avoided if possible in future. This is a directly visible unencrypted source notice, not a new cryptanalytic result. The literal misspellings and the trailing forwarding annotation are retained in the input record. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p227_C.png).

</details>
